title: Modifications to the classical rat aortic ring model to allow vascular degeneration studies
protocol: Sacrifice five-week-old Sprague-Dawley male rats by CO2 asphyxiation and cervical dislocation.
Disinfect the abdominal skin with Pursept A Xpress.
Lift the skin at the bottom of the abdomen with forceps.
Make an incision in the skin and underlying muscles using scissors.
Make a Y-shaped incision through the rat’s thoracic cage, starting at the previous incision and running up to the manubrium of the sternum.
Extend the Y-shaped incision on each side to the shoulders.
Push the ribs to the side to provide access to the heart and lungs.
Displace the heart and lungs to provide access to the aorta.
Cut the distal thoracic aorta with fine scissors while holding it with forceps.
Progressively cut alongside the vertebral column to excise the aorta from the rat.
Make an incision on each side just under the thoracic cage.
Push the ribs to access the intrathoracic organs (heart and lungs).
Cut the diaphragm, vena cava, and esophagus.
Displace the heart and lungs to clear the thoracic cavity.
Displace the stomach, liver, and intestines to clear the abdominal cavity.
Absorb blood using an absorbent tissue.
Identify the aorta as it is tightly bound to the vertebral column.
Cut the distal end of the aorta using fine scissors.
Hold the distal end of the aorta with fine forceps.
Cut the subaortic tissue with scissors.
Cut the aorta at the proximal end.
Place the aorta in a Falcon tube containing EBM.
Remove fibroadipose tissue from the aorta.
Remove intraluminal blood clot from the aorta.
Flush the inside of the aorta with EBM to clean it.
Cut the aorta into 1-mm wide rings.
Remove the fibroadipose tissue under a stereo microscope.
Remove any intraluminal blood clots with forceps.
Insert a 2.5-mL syringe with a 23G needle containing EBM into the aorta lumen.
Flush EBM into the aorta to remove intraluminal blood.
Cut the aorta into 1-mm wide rings using a sharp blade in a single straight motion.
Discard the most proximal and distal aortic rings.
Keep only the sharp-cut rings.
Prepare a small volume of collagen working solution immediately before use.
Mix 200 μL of collagen stock solution with 200 μL DMEM without glucose in a hemolysis tube.
Equilibrate the pH with a few microliters of 5 N NaOH.
The working volume of 1 mg/mL collagen solution is sufficient for embedding six rings.
Add a sufficient volume of 5 N NaOH to the DMEM solution.
Mix gently and homogenize the solution to avoid bubble formation.
Maintain the pH of the solution between 7 and 7.4 by adding minimal volumes of NaOH as needed.
Keep collagen stock solution, "DMEM, no glucose" medium, and prepared working solution on ice to prevent polymerization.
Mix 1 mg/mL working collagen solution.
Fill three wells at a time with 60 μL of the working collagen solution in a 96-well culture plate.
Keep the tube containing the working solution on ice between each pipetting step.
Gently pick up an aortic ring with forceps and dry it and the tips of the forceps with an absorbent tissue to remove excess medium.
Embed the aortic ring into a collagen-filled well before it polymerizes, placing the ring in the center of the well with the walls of the aortic vessel facing the bottom.
Embed the ring within 5 min following the addition of collagen to prevent polymerization.
Hold the ring for 30 s with forceps until the gel starts to polymerize if it does not stay in position.
Gently remove the forceps from the gel while checking that the ring stays still.
Add 200 μl PBS to all empty surrounding wells to prevent evaporation in wells of interest.
Incubate the plate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 30 min to allow complete collagen polymerization.
Start incubation of the first plate as soon as all wells have been filled with aortic rings.
Warm EBM Medium by adding a 1:1,000 volume of Primocin and heating it in a water bath at 37°C.
Add 150 μL of warmed medium to each well containing aortic rings.
Incubate the plate for four days at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Count sprouts every day from day 4 to day 8 under a bright field or phase-contrast inverted microscope with a 40× or 100× magnification.
Prepare EBM Medium with 1:1,000 Primocin and heat it in a water bath at 37°C.
Remove 130 μl of the old medium from each well.
Add 150 μl of fresh EBM Medium with 1:1,000 Primocin to each well.
Remove the culture medium from all the wells for fluorescence imaging.
Wash each culture well with 200 μL PBS three times.
Incubate for 15 minutes between each wash.
Fix the culture with 100 μL 4% formaldehyde for 30 minutes.
Wash each culture well with 200 μL PBS three times.
Incubate for 15 minutes between each wash.
Dilute primary IBA1 antibody at 1:200 in PBS 0.1% Triton X-100.
Incubate for 3 to 7 days at 4°C.
Wash three times with 200 μL PBS, incubating for 15 minutes each time.
Add secondary antibody at 1:400 and ISOLECTIN B4 treatment (10 μg/mL) in PBS.
Incubate for a minimum of 12 hours at 4°C.
Add Hoechst 33342 at 1:1,000 and incubate for an additional 30 minutes.
Wash three times with 200 μL PBS, incubating for 15 minutes each time.
